title: information boundary, strict feedback and termination semantics

activity.note: pure numpy module and pytest slice; no engine, no checkpoint, no shard

input_shapes.fixture_source: numpy.random.default_rng(20241113), synthetic pixels; no game frame and no D1 shard was read
input_shapes.privileged_keys_in_fixtures: all 17 PRIVILEGED_KEYS are forged with two different value sets to test invariance

checks.constraint: strict_observation returns exactly play, play_norm, hud, act_hist
non-array, wrong dtype or wrong shape raises ProtocolError through encode_observation
every privileged key, at any depth and in any letter case, raises ProtocolError
StrictPixelPolicy.logits accepts arrays only; logits_from_observation accepts exactly the four pixel keys
identical pixels/history give bit-identical move logits and bomb logit; no RNG, no globals, no instance state; unaffected by forged referee state
strict_feedback reads only death_visible, stage_clear_visible, game_over_visible, menu_visible, paused_visible, resource_delta, frame
privileged keys raise ProtocolError; ordinary unknown keys are ignored and appended to the optional record list; invalid types raise ProtocolError
precedence game_over > stage_clear > first_death > cap; a terminal event always overrides cap; invalid events/frame/cap raise ProtocolError
a menu/pause frame without terminal evidence raises ProtocolError and is never reported as survival or cap; explicit terminal evidence still wins
cap is returned only when no terminal pixel event is visible and frame >= cap; below cap with no event the classifier returns None
standard = S1N/RUNN natural starts; practice = PSN practice start points only; cross-use, duplicates, empty selection and unknown names raise ProtocolError
no function mutates its inputs; returned observation arrays are copies that never alias the caller buffers
the module launches no game, trains nothing, collects nothing and opens no sealed asset; it imports only stdlib, numpy and touhou_rl.v410 adapters/protocol
tests: module scope, verified by inspection of touhou_rl/v410/boundary.py imports

checks.constraint: boundary_report() is JSON-serialisable, carries design constraints only and states capability_claim=false for the stub

case_total_reconciliation.note: cases are attributed once; B13 is a design constraint with zero test cases, so the sum equals the pytest pass count

termination.cap_rule: cap only when no terminal pixel event is visible and frame >= cap
termination.menu_pause_rule: menu/pause frames are not alive: without terminal evidence they raise ProtocolError and are never reported as survival or cap
precedence_rationale: game_over is unconditional: a failed run must not be masked by a stale clear banner
stage_clear outranks a visible death animation on the same frame, because recording a cleared stage as a death would fabricate a failure
first_death ends an episode while resources remain
cap is a budget artefact and never overrides an observed event

resources.contract: practice start points are not comparable with standard natural starts; results from the two suites are never pooled

policy_stub.kind: deterministic fixed linear projection (splitmix64-derived constant weights)
policy_stub.status: interface stub, not a capability claim
policy_stub.forbidden: all PRIVILEGED_KEYS; logits_from_observation rejects any privileged key
policy_stub.statement: the stub exists to test the boundary interface; its determinism and privilege-blindness are properties of the code, not evidence of policy capability

corrections.detail: the first pytest run collected 151 cases and reported 150 passed / 1 failed because test_policy_rejects_wrong_encoded_dtypes used play_norm.reshape(4,112,95) on a 43008-element array; the test now slices [:, :, :95]

not_claimed: does not claim policy capability, convergence, win rate or sample efficiency
does not claim any engine, retail or real-time behaviour
does not claim that the pixel boundary is sufficient for learning, only that privileged fields are excluded
no game run, no training run and no data collection backs these numbers; the 151 cases are synthetic unit tests
limitations: StrictPixelPolicy is an interface stub with fixed weights and no training; it produces logits but says nothing about their quality
the feedback and termination rules are design decisions encoded here; they have not been validated against engine telemetry (none was collected)
strict_feedback assumes resource_delta and the *_visible flags are already measured from pixels by an external harness that this WP does not implement
menu/pause handling is fail-closed (ProtocolError) rather than a resume policy; the caller must handle frozen frames
resource suite validation checks names only; it cannot verify the actual in-game resources of a session
